title: Customer Churn Analysis Report
executive_summary: This report analyzes churn patterns across 749 customers. The overall churn rate stands at 37.7%. Critical risk factors include monthly contracts, which show a 121% higher churn rate than annual contracts, and a specific at-risk segment with high support ticket volume and low satisfaction, exhibiting a 71% churn rate. Lifetime value scales significantly with plan tier, offering potential for revenue growth through retention efforts.

key_findings.statement: The dataset comprises 749 customers with an overall churn rate of 37.7% and an average monthly fee of $42.11.
Churn rates are relatively consistent across plans, ranging from 36.6% (Premium) to 38.9% (Basic). The Basic plan has the highest churn rate.
Churn rates by signup cohort show minor variation, with the 2024 cohort having the highest churn rate at 39.8% and the 2022 cohort the lowest at 36.7%.
Monthly contract holders churn at a rate of 48.3%, compared to 21.9% for annual contract holders. This represents a 121.1% increase in churn rate for monthly contracts relative to annual ones.
An at-risk segment of 100 customers with high support tickets and low satisfaction exhibits a churn rate of 71.0%, nearly double the overall average.
Customer tenure averages 20.8 months (median 19.0, std dev 13.2). The average satisfaction score is 3.4, with 27 customers missing a satisfaction score.
Lifetime value (LTV) increases significantly by plan tier, with Premium LTV at $1,817 compared to Basic at $463. Premium LTV is 292.0% higher than Basic LTV.

limitations: The analysis is based on a single snapshot and does not capture time-series dynamics beyond signup cohorts.
Satisfaction scores were missing for 27 customers, which may bias the satisfaction mean.
Causality cannot be inferred; observed associations (e.g., contract type and churn) may be influenced by unobserved factors.
conclusion: To reduce churn, prioritize converting monthly customers to annual contracts and intervene with the high-support, low-satisfaction segment. The substantial LTV difference between Basic and Premium plans suggests that retention efforts focused on Premium customers could yield significant revenue protection.
